title: Validation report
description: The output of every validate skill, so results compose across experts. Three tiers, and only the first two are mechanical. A report that marks tier 3 passed is malformed, not reassuring: mechanical checks verify form, and whether an artifact faithfully represents its source is a human ruling.

skill.description: Skill id that produced this report.

source.description: Path to the L2 source it was derived from, where applicable.

sourceHashes.description: Twelve-character SHA-256 prefixes of the inputs at validation time, so this report expires when they change.

shape.description: T1. Does the artifact match its output schema.

conformance.description: T2. Definition of done statements, profile conformance, and round-trip completeness.

fidelity.description: T3. Does the artifact faithfully represent its source. Never auto-passed.

flags.description: Questions raised during validation that are not the validator's to close.

outcome.description: pass is only reachable once a person has ruled on fidelity. A report whose fidelity tier is still pending is requires-human, which is a complete and correct terminal state, not a failure.

result.description: Only a human ruling may set this to pass or fail. An automated validator writes requires-human.

ruledBy.description: Who ruled. Required when result is not requires-human.

comparisons.description: What the agent presents to the person: source beside output, with its reading of the difference. This is what makes the human step cheap rather than a full re-read.

reading.description: The agent's argument for why these correspond, or why they do not.

id.description: Requirement statement key where the check comes from one, otherwise a checker-defined id.

evidence.description: Required on any failing check. file:line plus a verbatim quote. A failure with nothing to point at is itself a defect.

metrics.description: Checker-defined counts. Useful for the failure mode where a run exits clean with implausible numbers.
